title: Microsoft launches its new AI model for making decisions quickly.
source_used: TestingCatalog (relaying Microsoft's announcement) and The Verge
key_facts: Microsoft announced Microsoft-Decision-1, a model built for fast decision scoring, available now in Microsoft Foundry and due on OpenRouter soon.
Instead of writing text, it takes a fixed set of options (yes/no, multiple choice, ratings) and returns a calibrated probability for each in one API call.
Microsoft post-trained the open Qwen3.5-9B model for this task.

Microsoft says it had the highest accuracy in a 36-benchmark test of nearly 150,000 held-out questions, 4.5 times faster than runner-up Quyet-1.0-Large and 35 times faster than GPT-6 Sol at median latency.
Microsoft says its decision changed 1.3% of the time across eight rewordings of the same request.
Pricing starts at $0.042 per million input tokens, with output tokens free.
The Verge notes the launch came days after OpenAI highlighted its new Decisions API.
quote_evidence: Microsoft has launched Microsoft-Decision-1, a purpose-built model for fast decision scoring that produces structured choices software can act on immediately.
Microsoft says the model achieved the highest accuracy in a 36-benchmark evaluation covering nearly 150,000 questions withheld from training.

Apparently, after large language models and agents, we're now in the age of "decision models," as Microsoft has announced Microsoft-Decision-1 just days after OpenAI highlighted its new Decisions API.
why_it_matters_hint: A low-cost control layer that tells software whether to act, retry or escalate could make AI agents cheaper to run.
notes: Microsoft's own post (commandline.microsoft.com) returned 403; the Verge page held only three sentences. Facts come from TestingCatalog, which relays Microsoft's announcement. All performance figures are Microsoft's own tests.
